title: Conditional Formatting and Data Validation
summary: Apply automatic cell formatting based on value rules, and restrict what users can enter into a cell.

steps.title: Highlighting Cells Automatically by Value
steps.lede: Conditional formatting applies a format to cells based on rules you create — no manual colouring needed.

blocks.text: Conditional formatting applies a format to cells automatically based on rules you create that determine the format based on the cells' values — rather than you manually colouring cells one at a time.

To apply a quick conditional formatting rule, select the cells, then on the Home tab in the Style group select Conditional Formatting > Highlight Cells Rules, choose a comparison command such as Less Than, enter the comparison value, and select a format. Selecting the delivery-time column and applying Highlight Cells Rules > Less Than with a value of 15 and a green fill automatically colours every delivery under 15 minutes.

blocks.change_summary: Home > Conditional Formatting > Highlight Cells Rules > Less Than, value 15, green fill — cells below 15 are automatically coloured; cells at or above 15 remain unformatted.

steps.title: Applying a Conditional Formatting Rule via Highlight Cells Rules

steps.title: Applying a Conditional Formatting Rule
steps.lede: Test your understanding of how to set up a Highlight Cells Rules rule.

public.prompt: You want to highlight all cells in the delivery_minutes column (C2:C21) that contain values below 30, using a red fill. Which sequence of steps achieves this?

options.text: Select C2:C21 → Home → Conditional Formatting → Highlight Cells Rules → Less Than → enter 30 → choose a red fill format.
Select C2:C21 → Insert → Conditional Formatting → Less Than → enter 30 → choose a red fill format.
Select C2:C21 → Home → Format Cells → Conditional → Less Than → enter 30 → choose a red fill format.
Select C2:C21 → Data → Conditional Formatting → Highlight Cells Rules → Less Than → enter 30 → choose a red fill format.

opt_b.message: Conditional Formatting is not on the Insert tab. It is on the Home tab, in the Styles group. The correct path is Home → Conditional Formatting → Highlight Cells Rules → Less Than.

opt_c.message: There is no Conditional option inside Format Cells. Conditional Formatting is a separate command on the Home tab: Home → Conditional Formatting → Highlight Cells Rules → Less Than.

opt_d.message: Conditional Formatting is not on the Data tab. It is on the Home tab, in the Styles group. The correct path is Home → Conditional Formatting → Highlight Cells Rules → Less Than.

correct.message: Correct! The path is Home → Conditional Formatting → Highlight Cells Rules → Less Than → enter 30 → choose the red fill format. The rule then applies the format automatically to any cell below 30.

incorrect.message: Conditional Formatting is on the Home tab (not Insert or Data). The path is: Home → Conditional Formatting → Highlight Cells Rules → Less Than → enter the threshold → choose the format.

hints: Conditional Formatting lives on the Home tab, in the Styles group — not on Insert or Data.
The Highlight Cells Rules submenu contains comparison commands like Less Than, Greater Than, and Equal To.

steps.title: Apply a Conditional Formatting Rule
steps.lede: Apply a Highlight Cells Rules rule to the delivery_minutes column to flag values above a threshold.

public.prompt: You want to highlight all cells in the delivery_minutes column (C2:C21) that contain values less than 30. In cell F1, write a formula that returns TRUE if the value in C2 is less than 30, and FALSE otherwise. This formula logic is what a conditional formatting rule would use to determine which cells to highlight.

correct.message: Correct! =C2<30 returns TRUE because 28 is less than 30. In conditional formatting, you would use Home → Conditional Formatting → Highlight Cells Rules → Less Than to apply this logic to the entire range C2:C21, highlighting all cells where the value is less than 30.

incorrect.message: Write a formula that compares C2 to 30: =C2<30. This returns TRUE if the value is less than 30, FALSE otherwise.

hints: Use the less than operator (<) to compare C2 to 30.
The formula should return TRUE or FALSE based on whether the value meets the condition.

steps.title: Restricting What Users Can Enter
steps.lede: Data validation restricts the type of data or values users can enter into a cell, and can display a custom error message.

blocks.text: Data validation restricts the type of data or the values users can enter into a cell, such as a dropdown list, and can display a customised error message when a user enters invalid data.

To add a dropdown-list validation rule, select the cells, choose Data > Data Validation, on the Settings tab set Allow to List, then in the Source box type the list values separated by commas, making sure the In-cell dropdown check box is selected. Restricting the Orders sheet's status column with Source set to Pending,Delivered,Cancelled gives each cell a dropdown of those three words.

blocks.title: Data Validation dialog — Settings tab for a List restriction

nodes.label: Set Allow to List to create a dropdown restriction.
Type the allowed values separated by commas. These become the dropdown options.
The cell now shows a dropdown arrow; only the three listed values are accepted.

blocks.alt_text: Diagram of the Data Validation dialog open on the Settings tab with Allow set to List and the Source box containing 'Pending,Delivered,Cancelled'. A callout points to a Status column cell showing a dropdown arrow. Labels explain each dialog field.

steps.title: Numeric, Date, and Text-Length Validation
steps.lede: Data validation can also restrict entry to a number, date, or text of a specific length.

blocks.text: Data validation can restrict entry to a whole number, decimal, date, time, or text length within limits: under Allow choose the type (for example Whole Number), under Data choose a condition (for example between), and then enter the minimum, maximum, or specific value to allow. On the delivery-time column, choosing Whole Number, between 0 and 300, blocks anyone from typing a negative or unreasonably large delivery time.

steps.title: Restricting Cell Input: Error Alerts and Numeric Rules
steps.lede: See how the Allow menu switches between types and how error alerts work.

segments.label: Input messages, error alerts, and numeric/date/text-length validation rules
segments.summary: The instructor selects a cell that already has a dropdown rule and opens Data Validation to add an input message ('Please make a selection from the list') and a custom error alert, showing that without a custom message Excel displays a default restriction notice, and with one it shows the custom text instead. The instructor then opens Data Validation for a date column, chooses the Date type with a 'greater than today' condition using the TODAY function, adds an input message and a custom alert, and demonstrates that a past date is rejected while a future date is accepted. Next, a project-number column is restricted to Whole Number, between 1,000 and 2,000, with the error alert noting the allowed range. A company-code column is then restricted using Text Length equal to 5, confirming that a five-character entry passes and a six-character entry fails. Finally, a project-description column is restricted to Text Length greater than 20, so a short phrase is rejected and a longer one is accepted. A brief aside notes that a Custom formula option exists for pattern-based rules but is deferred as an advanced topic.

steps.title: Data Validation Purpose and Numeric Rules
steps.lede: Test your understanding of what data validation does and how to configure a numeric rule.

public.prompt: You want to restrict the delivery_minutes column so that only whole numbers between 1 and 300 can be entered. In the Data Validation dialog, which settings achieve this?

options.text: Allow: Whole Number; Data: between; Minimum: 1; Maximum: 300.
Allow: Decimal; Data: between; Minimum: 1; Maximum: 300.
Allow: Text Length; Data: between; Minimum: 1; Maximum: 300.

opt_b.message: Decimal allows fractional numbers (e.g., 45.5). To restrict to whole numbers only, choose Whole Number, not Decimal.

opt_c.message: List creates a dropdown with specific values. To allow any whole number in a range, choose Whole Number with a between condition and set the minimum and maximum.

opt_d.message: Text Length restricts the number of characters in a text entry, not the numeric value. To restrict to whole numbers between 1 and 300, choose Whole Number with a between condition.

correct.message: Correct! Allow: Whole Number; Data: between; Minimum: 1; Maximum: 300 restricts the cell to whole numbers in that range. Any entry outside the range triggers the error message.

incorrect.message: To allow only whole numbers between 1 and 300, set Allow to Whole Number, Data to between, Minimum to 1, and Maximum to 300.

hints: The Allow dropdown determines the type of data permitted. For whole numbers, choose Whole Number (not Decimal or Text Length).
The Data dropdown sets the condition (between, greater than, less than, etc.). For a range, choose between and set the minimum and maximum.

steps.title: Choosing the Right Validation Type
steps.lede: Given an input restriction requirement, identify the correct validation type to use.

public.prompt: A colleague wants to restrict the status column so that users can only enter one of three values: Delivered, Pending, or Cancelled. Which validation type should they choose?

options.text: List — because it creates a dropdown with the exact allowed values, preventing any other entry.
Whole Number — because the status values can be coded as numbers (1, 2, 3).
Text Length — because each status value has a specific character count.
Decimal — because status values can be represented as decimal codes.

opt_b.message: Whole Number restricts entries to numeric values within a range. It cannot enforce specific text values like 'Delivered'. Use List to restrict entries to a fixed set of text options.

opt_c.message: Text Length restricts the number of characters, not the specific text. 'Delivered' (9 chars) and 'Cancelled' (9 chars) have the same length, so Text Length cannot distinguish between them. Use List instead.

opt_d.message: Decimal restricts entries to numeric values. It cannot enforce specific text values like 'Pending'. Use List to create a dropdown with the allowed text values.

correct.message: Correct! List validation creates a dropdown showing the allowed values (Delivered, Pending, Cancelled) and prevents any other entry. It is the right choice when you need to restrict input to a fixed set of text options.

incorrect.message: When you need to restrict input to a fixed set of text values, use List validation. It creates a dropdown with the allowed options and blocks any other entry.

hints: List validation is designed for exactly this scenario: a fixed set of allowed values shown as a dropdown.
Whole Number and Decimal are for numeric ranges; Text Length is for character counts. None of those can enforce specific text values.

steps.title: Add a Dropdown Validation Rule to the Status Column
steps.lede: Restrict the Status column to Pending, Delivered, and Cancelled using Data > Data Validation.

public.prompt: You want to restrict the status column (E2:E21) so that users can only enter Delivered, Pending, or Cancelled. In cell G1, write a formula that returns TRUE if the value in E2 is one of these three allowed values, and FALSE otherwise. Use arithmetic and comparison operators: =(E2="Delivered")+(E2="Pending")+(E2="Cancelled")>0

correct.message: Correct! =(E2="Delivered")+(E2="Pending")+(E2="Cancelled")>0 returns TRUE because E2 contains "Delivered", which is one of the allowed values. Each comparison returns 1 (TRUE) or 0 (FALSE); adding them gives a count of matches, and >0 checks if at least one match exists. In data validation, you would use Data → Data Validation → Allow: List with Source set to Delivered,Pending,Cancelled to create a dropdown that restricts entry to these three values.

incorrect.message: Use arithmetic and comparison operators to check if E2 equals any of the three allowed values: =(E2="Delivered")+(E2="Pending")+(E2="Cancelled")>0. Each comparison returns 1 or 0; adding them counts matches; >0 checks if any match exists.

hints: Each comparison like E2="Delivered" returns TRUE (1) or FALSE (0). Adding three comparisons counts how many match.
Use quotes around text values: E2="Delivered". The full formula is =(E2="Delivered")+(E2="Pending")+(E2="Cancelled")>0.

steps.title: Conditional Formatting and Data Validation — Key Points
steps.lede: You can now apply automatic cell formatting rules and restrict what users can enter.

blocks.text: Conditional formatting applies a format to cells automatically based on rules you create from cell values. Use Home > Conditional Formatting > Highlight Cells Rules, choose a comparison such as Less Than, enter the threshold, and pick a format. Data validation restricts what users can enter: choose Data > Data Validation, set Allow to List and type comma-separated values for a dropdown, or choose Whole Number, Date, or Text Length with a condition and limits for numeric restrictions. A customised error message can be shown when invalid data is entered.

remediation_steps.title: Setting Up a Highlight Cells Rule
remediation_steps.lede: Walk through the exact menu path and see the rule trigger automatically.

blocks.text: Conditional formatting applies a format automatically based on cell values — you do not colour cells manually. To apply a Less Than rule to the delivery-time column: select the column cells, go to Home > Conditional Formatting > Highlight Cells Rules > Less Than, type 15 in the value box, choose a red fill, and click OK. Every cell whose value is below 15 is immediately coloured red; cells at or above 15 remain unformatted. The rule re-evaluates whenever a cell value changes.

remediation_steps.title: What Data Validation Does and How to Set Numeric Limits
remediation_steps.lede: Data validation blocks invalid input before it reaches the cell.

blocks.text: Data validation restricts the type of data or the values users can enter into a cell, and can display a customised error message when a user enters invalid data. For a numeric restriction on the delivery-time column: select the column, choose Data > Data Validation, set Allow to Whole Number, set Data to between, enter 0 as the minimum and 300 as the maximum, and click OK. Typing a negative number or a value above 300 triggers the restriction notice.

remediation_steps.title: Choosing the Right Validation Type
remediation_steps.lede: Match the input restriction requirement to the correct Allow setting.

blocks.text: Use List when you want to restrict entry to a fixed set of text values — for example, Pending, Delivered, Cancelled in the status column. Use Whole Number or Decimal when you want to restrict entry to a number within a range — for example, delivery times between 0 and 300. Use Date or Time for date or time restrictions. Use Text Length when you want to restrict how many characters can be entered. All types are set through Data > Data Validation > Settings > Allow.
